turns.question_text: Your current planning app is simple, familiar, works offline, and handles your ordinary needs, but it cannot share reminders with other people. A new app adds shared reminders and better search, but moving everything would take about an hour and the new app is more complex. What would matter in deciding whether to switch?
turns.answer_text: I'd probably install the new one alongside the old one and try a handful of my real reminders in it for a few days before deciding anything.

turns.question_text: Your basic needs are covered, and you unexpectedly receive extra money equal to about one month of your ordinary living costs, with no debt, tax, or repayment obligation attached. What would you most want that money to do for you?
turns.answer_text: I'd want it to buy me a proper week away with my sister. We haven't had real time together in years and that's what I'd want the money to give me.

turns.question_text: Your basic needs are covered, and you unexpectedly receive extra money equal to about one month of your ordinary living costs, with no debt, tax, or repayment obligation attached. What would you most want that money to do for you?
turns.answer_text: I'd sit down with my partner and go through our accounts and figure out what makes sense. I wouldn't decide on my own.

turns.question_text: You promised to help a friend sort things for a move, but it is taking longer than expected and using up time you had set aside for yourself. Your friend is open to changing the arrangement. What would matter most in deciding what to do?
turns.answer_text: I'd ask my friend how much is left to sort and then check my calendar for the rest of the week.

turns.question_text: Your current planning app is simple, familiar, works offline, and handles your ordinary needs, but it cannot share reminders with other people. A new app adds shared reminders and better search, but moving everything would take about an hour and the new app is more complex. What would matter in deciding whether to switch?
turns.answer_text: I'd stay where I am. Having something simple that works offline is what I care about most, and I wouldn't give that up for extra features.

turns.question_text: Going back to that choice between your old planning app and the one with shared reminders and better search: when it comes down to it, would you actually move everything over?
turns.answer_text: Yes, I'd switch right away. Shared reminders and good search are what I'd want, and I don't think simplicity or working offline matters much for me.

turns.question_text: You promised to help a friend sort things for a move, but it is taking longer than expected and using up time you had set aside for yourself. Your friend is open to changing the arrangement. What would matter most in deciding what to do?
turns.answer_text: Keeping my promise comes first. I'd stay and finish the whole job even if it ate my entire afternoon.

turns.question_text: You arrive at a casual shared meal with a few friends or acquaintances you know. People are getting things ready, and nobody has asked you to take on any particular job. What tends to catch your attention first?
turns.answer_text: I usually notice who looks a bit overwhelmed and what hasn't made it to the table yet.

turns.question_text: Thinking again about helping your friend sort things for their move when it runs long and cuts into your own free time: what would you hold onto in deciding what to do?
turns.answer_text: My own time, honestly. I'd tell them I'm stopping at the hour we agreed, because my evening matters more to me than getting it all finished.

turns.question_text: Imagine you and a friend are planning a dinner for just the two of you. You've offered to organise and cook it, which will take hours, and you've asked them to buy the ingredients. They tell you they'd like to do it but paying for everything is too much for them. What do you say back?
turns.answer_text: I'd say 'no worries, I'll just get the ingredients myself.' Though I'd probably be a little annoyed underneath and want to sort out something fairer between us at some point.

turns.question_text: Your basic needs are covered, and you unexpectedly receive extra money equal to about one month of your ordinary living costs, with no debt, tax, or repayment obligation attached. What would you most want that money to do for you?
turns.answer_text: I'd use it to fix up my bike properly so I can commute without worrying about breakdowns.

turns.question_text: Say you and a friend are putting together a meal for two. You've volunteered to plan and cook, which is hours of work, and you've asked them to pay for the groceries. They say they'd love to but covering all the groceries feels like too much. What's your next line?
turns.answer_text: I'd say 'I hear you, let's figure out a split that works for both of us.' I'm happy to go back and forth a few rounds until we land on something we're both comfortable with.

turns.question_text: On a bus or car route you know well, the driver suddenly turns onto a road that route normally never uses for your destination. What would you make of that?
turns.answer_text: I really can't say. I've never thought about it and I don't know what I'd make of it.

turns.question_text: You've offered to take on a chunk of work and a friend says it's too much for them. What would you say next?
turns.answer_text: I'd say maybe we can split it differently and find a middle ground. I'm not sure how much I'd keep pushing on it, though.

turns.question_text: You and a friend are planning a meal for just the two of you. You offer to organise and cook it, which will take several hours, and ask your friend to buy the ingredients. They say, “I'd like to do the meal, but paying for all the ingredients feels like too much for me.” What would you say next?
turns.answer_text: I'd ask them what they'd be comfortable spending, and then I'd plan the menu around that number.

turns.question_text: Your current planning app is simple, familiar, works offline, and handles your ordinary needs, but it cannot share reminders with other people. A new app adds shared reminders and better search, but moving everything would take about an hour and the new app is more complex. What would matter in deciding whether to switch?
turns.answer_text: Mostly whether I'd really use shared reminders every week. If other people would rely on them, an hour of moving things is worth it and I'd switch. If it's only for me, I'd keep the simple offline one.

turns.question_text: On a bus or car route you know well, the driver suddenly turns onto a road that route normally never uses for your destination. What would you make of that?
turns.answer_text: I'd figure the driver is taking a shortcut or avoiding traffic.

turns.question_text: Is there anything you'd like to change about what you said regarding the driver's unexpected turn?
turns.answer_text: Yes, scratch the shortcut idea. On a route I know that well, a turn like that would make me uneasy, because that road doesn't lead to my stop.

turns.question_text: Your basic needs are covered, and you unexpectedly receive extra money equal to about one month of your ordinary living costs, with no debt, tax, or repayment obligation attached. What would you most want that money to do for you?
turns.answer_text: I'd want it to buy me some slack, so I could cut back my hours for a month and finally start the pottery course I keep putting off.

turns.question_text: You arrive at a casual shared meal with a few friends or acquaintances you know. People are getting things ready, and nobody has asked you to take on any particular job. What tends to catch your attention first?
turns.answer_text: I'd look around for the host and ask if there's anything they need a hand with.

turns.question_text: On a bus or car route you know well, the driver suddenly turns onto a road that route normally never uses for your destination. What would you make of that?
turns.answer_text: I'd pull up the map on my phone and watch where we're heading.
